maps.description: The standard's file entry example: the greetings tree as text, Base64 and hash entries, whose digest is the tree's whichever form each file travels in.
A string entry's bytes are its UTF-8 encoding exactly: no line ending converted, no byte order mark added or removed, a NUL kept.
An empty file travels as an empty string, an empty Base64 string or the hash of no bytes.
A Base64 entry carries any bytes.
A hash entry resolves in the receiver's blob store, beside inline entries.
A tree path may hold spaces, accents, a non-Latin script and URL punctuation: it is a name, never a storage location.
A file named node_modules or __pycache__ is a member, and so is METHODS.toml at the root.
A segment of exactly 255 bytes is valid.

maps.description: Two directories differing only in letter case, with no two paths equal once case-folded, are accepted.
A map with no key is refused: a tree holds at least one file.
A key given twice in the document text is refused, rather than one of its values kept.
A key given twice, once through a JSON escape, is the same key and is refused.
A key given twice inside a Base64 entry object is refused as a duplicate key, naming the map key, even when both values agree.
A key given twice inside a hash entry object is refused as a duplicate key, naming the map key.
A key not in NFC is not a tree path.
A key must already be in NFC: beside café.txt, the key café.txt is no tree path, and the pair is no duplicate.
A key holding a segment that starts with a dot is refused: no tree has such a member.
A key under a dot directory is refused.
A key with a .. segment is not a tree path.
A key with a . segment is not a tree path.
A .. segment inside a key is not a tree path either.
An absolute key is not a tree path.
A key ending with / is not a tree path.
A key with an empty segment is not a tree path.
A key holding a backslash is not a tree path.
A key holding a colon is not a tree path.
A key holding NUL is not a tree path.
A key holding a line feed is not a tree path.
A key holding U+007F is not a tree path.
A key holding a C1 control character is not a tree path.
A key holding a lone surrogate, which UTF-8 cannot encode, is not a tree path.
A key with a segment of 256 bytes is not a tree path.
A key of 1025 bytes is not a tree path.
A key inside a __pycache__ directory is refused.
A key inside a node_modules directory is refused.
A key naming a file pyvenv.cfg is refused.
A key naming pyvenv.cfg at the root is refused too.
A key naming METHODS.toml anywhere but at the root is refused.
A key naming a run's inputs file inputs.json at the root is refused: no tree has such a member.
A key naming a run's inputs file inputs.toml at the root is refused.
A key whose last segment is inputs.json is refused below the root too.
A directory named inputs.json or inputs.toml excludes nothing: keys under it are members.
The run-inputs names match byte for byte: Inputs.json and INPUTS.TOML are members.
A key inputs.json beside Inputs.json is refused as excluded_name alone: a key refused as excluded_name takes no part in the collision check, so Inputs.json collides with nothing.
Two keys equal once case-folded are refused, naming both.
A key naming a directory of another once both are case-folded is refused.
A key naming a directory of another key is refused, letter case aside.
Case folding covers every script.
Full case folding folds ß into ss.
The capital sharp s ẞ and the small ß fold together.
Full case folding folds the final sigma ς into σ.
Full case folding folds the long s ſ into s.
No entry names a file by URL, or by any key but base64, or sha256 with size.
An entry object holds no other key.
An entry takes exactly one form.
An entry is a string or an object.
An entry is never null.
An entry is never an array.
An empty object is no entry form.
Base64 is padded.
Base64 holds no line break.
Base64 uses the standard alphabet, not the URL-safe one.
Base64 must be canonical: aGl= has padding bits that are not zero, though a lenient decoder reads it as hi.
Base64 must be canonical: YR== has padding bits that are not zero, though a lenient decoder reads it as a.
A Base64 value is a string.
A hash is lowercase hexadecimal.
A hash is 64 hexadecimal digits.
A size is a non-negative integer.
A size is a number, not a string.
A size is a number, not a boolean.
A size is an integer.
A size is a JSON integer written without a fraction: 13.0 is refused though it equals the held size.
A size is a JSON integer written without an exponent: 1.3e1 is refused though it equals the held size.
A string entry holding a lone surrogate, which UTF-8 cannot encode, is refused.
A hash entry the receiver's blob store does not hold is refused, naming the hash.
Every hash entry the receiver lacks is named at once, as the protocol's missing_blobs lists them, so a sender learns in one answer what to upload.
A hash entry whose size differs from the held bytes' is refused like a missing blob, naming the hash.

paths.description: A segment may start with a dot: the tree path rules allow it, and only the membership rule keeps such a file out of a tree.
A run's inputs file is a tree path: the tree path rules allow it, and only the membership rule keeps such a file out of a tree.
A segment made of three dots is neither . nor ..
Two dots inside a segment are allowed.
Leading and trailing spaces are allowed.
URL punctuation is allowed in a name.
A no-break space is of category Zs, not a control character.
U+FEFF is of category Cf, not a control character.
U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR is of category Zl, not Cc, so it is allowed.
A character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane is allowed.
